strengths: Addresses a practical and important problem in efficient 3D reconstruction with significant computational benefits (400× speedup)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including multiple metrics, ablation studies, in-domain and out-of-domain settings, and cross-model evaluation with NeRF and 3DGS
Strong empirical results consistently outperforming baselines while using only half the viewpoints, achieving performance comparable to upper bound
Demonstrates generalization to unseen object categories without requiring retraining
Contributes a substantial Neural Uncertainty Map dataset with 62,400 image-UMap pairs that could benefit the community
Clear interpretability of predicted uncertainty maps with semantic visualization
Well-structured experimental setup with fair comparisons using identical configurations across methods
weaknesses: Severely restricted scope limiting practical applicability: assumes single objects with fixed spherical viewpoint distribution (fixed radius r=2.73) and cannot handle complex scenes, multi-object environments, or arbitrary viewpoint distributions
All evaluation restricted to synthetic ShapeNet data with no real-world experiments or validation on actual 3D objects

Ground-truth uncertainty maps depend entirely on pre-trained SplatterImage model quality, creating circular dependency where the method learns to predict one model's errors rather than intrinsic geometric uncertainty
Missing comparisons with recent 3DGS-based AVS methods (ActiveSplat, ActiveGS, ActiveGAMER) despite citing them, only comparing against older methods

Key methodological choices lack justification: multiplicative aggregation (Eq. 2) bounded by minimum uncertainty is potentially overly conservative; 0.1 redundancy threshold appears arbitrary with no ablation; 30° interpolation radius unexplained
Limited technical novelty: essentially fine-tuning standard ViT to predict 48-dim vector followed by simple interpolation and max-selection; each component is straightforward
Insufficient analysis of learned representations: only two uncertainty map examples shown; no systematic analysis of what UPNet learns, failure modes, or when it succeeds/fails
Significant domain shift between training (48 anchor viewpoints) and inference (512 random candidate viewpoints) not thoroughly analyzed
Only 2 out-of-domain categories tested (car, chair); unclear how generalization scales to more diverse object categories
Evaluation claims about generalization to 'diverse neural rendering models' limited to two volumetric representations (NeRF and 3DGS); unclear applicability to mesh-based or other architectures

strengths: Elegant and well-motivated solution to computational bottleneck in AVS: directly predicting uncertainty maps eliminates costly iterative NeRF retraining
Impressive practical efficiency: 400× speedup in viewpoint selection with 50%+ reduction in computational resources (CPU, RAM, GPU)

Strong empirical results: consistently outperforms baselines across 8 diverse metrics (image quality, mesh quality, visual coverage) while achieving near upper-bound performance with only half the viewpoints
Effective cross-model generalization: viewpoints selected by PUN work well across different neural rendering models (NeRF and 3DGS), demonstrating robustness
Valuable dataset contribution: NUM dataset with 62,400 viewpoint-uncertainty map pairs across 13 categories with proper train/val/test splits

Comprehensive experimental validation: fair comparisons with consistent hardware, identical splits, multiple runs with standard deviations, and thorough ablations on uncertainty metrics, selection policies, and dataset composition
Good generalization to unseen object categories: strong OOD performance despite training only on 11 categories
Interpretable uncertainty maps: visualizations reveal meaningful patterns (e.g., object symmetry exploitation) that provide insights into model behavior
Well-presented paper: clear motivation (teapot example), logical flow, effective figures, and accessible writing
weaknesses: Limited scope: restricted to single isolated objects with fixed spherical viewpoint distribution; cannot handle complex scenes, multiple objects, or large-scale 3D environments

Heuristic-based uncertainty metrics: ground truth relies on image-level metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, MSE) that may not fully reflect geometric fidelity or true viewpoint informativeness; acknowledged but not addressed

Incomplete generalization analysis: while UPNet generalizes to different rendering models at test time, it is trained exclusively on Splatter-Image-generated uncertainty maps; generalization to uncertainty from other synthesis methods is unexplored

Arbitrary design choices with limited justification: redundancy threshold (0.1) and multiplicative aggregation (Eq. 2) appear ad-hoc; no theoretical analysis of potential numerical issues or parameter sensitivity beyond brief ablations
Absence of failure case analysis: only successful examples shown (Fig. 3); no discussion of failure modes, challenging scenarios, or systematic analysis of problematic object categories
Overlooked data generation cost: paper emphasizes inference efficiency but does not discuss computational expense of creating NUM dataset (training multiple view synthesis models per object)
Limited baseline comparisons: only 3 recent baselines compared; some recently proposed methods (ActiveSplat, ActiveGS, ActiveGAMER) and RL-based approaches from related work not directly compared

Narrow out-of-domain evaluation: OOD testing uses only 2 held-out categories from the same distribution; true generalization would involve different object types or alternative 3D datasets (e.g., CO3D, Objaverse)
Incremental technical novelty: UPNet is standard architecture (ViT + FC); core contribution is engineering (learning to predict rather than compute) rather than methodological innovation
Missing statistical rigor: no formal significance testing despite having standard deviations; uncertainty interpolation and aggregation lack numerical stability analysis

strengths: Well-motivated approach to a real problem: replaces expensive iterative neural rendering model retraining with direct uncertainty prediction, achieving 400× speedup with significant practical benefits

Comprehensive and rigorous experimental evaluation: 6 datasets, 8 metrics spanning image/mesh/coverage quality, proper ablation studies, generalization to novel categories and reconstruction backbones
Strong empirical results: matches upper bound performance with ~50% of views, demonstrates generalization without retraining, and achieves dramatic resource reductions (50%+ CPU/RAM/GPU usage)
Useful dataset contribution: NUM dataset with 62.4k viewpoint-uncertainty map pairs across 13 categories and systematic ablations on dataset composition
Excellent reproducibility: detailed implementation details, promised code/model/dataset release, clear methodology enabling reproduction
weaknesses: Limited architectural and methodological novelty: UPNet is a standard ViT+MLP, uncertainty aggregation uses basic multiplication without principled justification, redundancy filtering via simple thresholding

Questionable theoretical foundation: no formal justification for why single-view 3DGS reconstruction error should predict multi-view performance; moderate correlations with complexity metrics (0.25-0.60) suggest the relationship is empirical rather than fundamental

Restrictive assumptions limiting applicability: method assumes spherical viewpoint distribution on fixed-radius hemisphere, fixed camera-object distance, and object-centric scenarios; acknowledged but severely limits real-world deployment

Limited real-world validation: training on 13 synthetic ShapeNet categories; real-world evaluation on only 8 scenes total (4 NeRFAssets + 4 MIP360) with smaller performance margins; no testing on significantly different object types

Experimental setup concerns: upper bound uses train/test overlap (40 evaluation poses for training) artificially inflating comparison; baselines optimized for different objectives while PUN trained on PSNR; fairness of comparison could be improved

Incomplete methodological analysis: no explanation for why multiplicative aggregation outperforms alternatives; claims about UPNet learning 'viewpoint difficulty' supported only by moderate correlations; missing failure case analysis

Dataset and reproducibility gaps: promised code/dataset URL incomplete in manuscript; computational cost of NUM generation not discussed; no sensitivity analysis for design choices like 30° interpolation threshold and 0.1 redundancy threshold

Questionable generalization claims: all test categories share structural properties with training data; limited evidence for generalization to fundamentally different object classes (articulated, deformable, very large/small objects)
